title: Lisbon Tops European City Search Rankings for Summer 2026 — What It Means for Travel Content
summary: Lisbon has surged to the #1 spot in European city search rankings for summer 2026, up 34% year-over-year. Travel content creators covering Portugal are seeing outsized organic traffic gains, particularly for shoulder-season and slow-travel formats.
content:
Skyscanner's latest travel demand data confirms Lisbon as the most-searched European city for summer 2026, with a 34% year-over-year increase in flight search queries. The surge is attributed to a combination of digital nomad visa uptake, cultural tourism recovery, and strong social media momentum from creator content published in Q1 2026.

For travel content creators, the data signals a significant organic search opportunity. Articles and videos targeting Lisbon shoulder-season travel (May–June, September–October) are outperforming peak-summer content in click-through rates, suggesting audiences are actively seeking alternatives to crowded July–August windows.

Slow-travel formats — multi-day neighborhood guides, local food itineraries, and 'live like a local' content — are performing especially well across Pinterest and YouTube. Creators with existing Portugal content are advised to refresh metadata and internal linking structures to capture the demand spike.

The Azores are emerging as a secondary beneficiary, with search volume up 41% since January 2026, presenting an extension opportunity for creators already established in the Portugal content niche.

title: FTC Reaffirms Disclosure Rules for Newsletter Affiliate Links — 'Clear and Conspicuous' Now Covers Email Footers
summary: The FTC has issued updated guidance confirming that influencer disclosure requirements apply to affiliate links in email newsletters, including footer placements. The 'clear and conspicuous' standard now explicitly covers email-based content monetization.
content:
The Federal Trade Commission released updated enforcement guidance this week clarifying that its influencer disclosure rules — long applied to social media and blog content — extend fully to email newsletter affiliate links. The guidance specifically addresses footer-only disclosures, ruling that a disclosure buried in an email footer does not meet the 'clear and conspicuous' standard if the affiliate link appears in the body of the newsletter without an adjacent disclosure.

Key takeaways for newsletter creators:
1. Affiliate links in newsletter body copy must be accompanied by a disclosure in close proximity — ideally immediately before or after the link.
2. A single footer disclosure is insufficient if multiple affiliate links appear throughout the email.
3. The guidance applies regardless of whether the creator is compensated per click, per sale, or through a flat-rate affiliate arrangement.

The FTC noted it will prioritize enforcement actions against creators with audiences over 10,000 subscribers, though the rules apply at all audience sizes. Industry groups including the Creator Economy Association are urging members to audit their newsletter templates before June 2026.

For creators running bundled sponsorship packages that include affiliate components, the guidance reinforces the importance of per-link disclosure rather than relying on a single sponsor acknowledgment block.

title: Tourism New Zealand Open Call: Content Creators for South Island Press Trip — August 2026
summary: Tourism New Zealand is accepting applications from travel content creators for a 10-day South Island itinerary press trip departing August 2026. Eligible creators must have 10K+ engaged following across primary platforms. Application deadline: June 30, 2026.
content:
Tourism New Zealand has issued an open call for travel content creators to participate in a hosted 10-day South Island itinerary press trip, with departure windows available in August 2026.

Eligibility criteria:
- Minimum 10,000 engaged followers/subscribers across primary content platform(s)
- Demonstrated travel content focus (blog, newsletter, YouTube, or Instagram)
- Previous press trip experience preferred but not required
- Must be able to produce and publish content within 60 days of trip completion

Deliverables expected:
- Minimum 2 long-form content pieces (article, video, or newsletter feature)
- Social media coverage during the trip (stories/reels encouraged)
- Full FTC-compliant disclosure on all published content

The itinerary covers Queenstown, Fiordland National Park, the Catlins, and Christchurch. Accommodation, domestic transport, and most meals are covered. International flights are the creator's responsibility.

Applications must include: media kit, audience demographics, links to three recent travel content pieces, and a brief pitch (200 words max) on your editorial angle for New Zealand content.

Deadline: June 30, 2026. Apply at: tourismnewzealand.example/creator-press-trips

Contact: pressoffice@tourismnz.govt.example

title: Substack Travel Newsletters Among Fastest-Growing Categories in Q1 2026 — Platform Reports 4.2% Paid Conversion Rate
summary: Substack's Q1 2026 growth report identifies travel as a top-5 fastest-growing newsletter category. Average paid subscriber conversion rate for travel content sits at 4.2%, above the platform-wide average of 3.1%.
content:
Substack's quarterly growth report for Q1 2026 highlights travel newsletters as one of the platform's five fastest-growing content categories, with new travel publication launches up 38% compared to Q1 2025.

Key metrics from the report:
- Average paid conversion rate for travel newsletters: 4.2% (vs. 3.1% platform-wide average)
- Top-performing travel newsletters average 2.3 paid posts per week
- Newsletters combining destination content with practical travel tips (packing, budgeting, booking strategy) show the highest paid conversion rates
- Geographic focus newsletters (single-country or single-region) outperform general travel newsletters in subscriber retention

Substack noted that travel creators who migrated from Mailchimp or ConvertKit in 2025 are seeing an average 18% increase in open rates, attributed to Substack's recommendation algorithm surfacing content to relevant readers.

For creators considering platform diversification, the report suggests that a Substack presence alongside an existing email platform can serve as a discovery channel, with readers often subscribing to the creator's primary list after finding them through Substack recommendations.

The platform is also expanding its 'Substack for Creators' grant program, with a travel-specific cohort planned for Q3 2026.

title: Visit Scotland Open Call: Creators for Highland & Islands Itinerary — Deadline May 28
summary: Visit Scotland is seeking solo and couple travel content creators for a hosted Highland & Islands itinerary trip in July–August 2026. Editorial pitch and audience demographics required. Application deadline: May 28, 2026.
content:
Visit Scotland has opened applications for a hosted press trip covering the Scottish Highlands and Islands, targeting solo and couple travel content creators with an editorial focus on outdoor adventure, cultural heritage, or sustainable travel.

Trip details:
- Destination: Scottish Highlands, Isle of Skye, Outer Hebrides
- Travel window: July–August 2026 (flexible within window)
- Duration: 8 days / 7 nights
- Coverage: Accommodation, ground transport, select meals
- Flights: Creator's responsibility (Edinburgh or Inverness gateway)

Application requirements:
- Editorial pitch (300 words max) outlining your content angle for Scotland
- Audience demographics (screenshot or analytics export acceptable)
- Links to 2–3 recent travel content pieces
- Confirmation of FTC/ASA disclosure compliance

Visit Scotland is particularly interested in creators whose audiences skew toward the US, Canada, Australia, and Germany — their primary target markets for 2026 inbound tourism campaigns.

Deadline: May 28, 2026
Apply via: visitscotland.example/trade/press-trips
Contact: mediaenquiries@visitscotland.example

Note: This is a hosted trip with no cash fee. Content must be published within 90 days of trip completion.

title: Booking.com Affiliate Creator Dashboard Beta — Real-Time Conversion Tracking Now Available
summary: Booking.com is rolling out a new 'Creator Dashboard' for affiliate partners, offering real-time conversion tracking, audience segmentation data, and optimized link formats. Beta access requires 10K+ monthly unique referrals.
content:
Booking.com has begun rolling out a new Creator Dashboard for its affiliate program, offering a significant upgrade over the existing reporting interface. The dashboard provides real-time conversion tracking, breaking down performance by content type (newsletter, blog post, social media), device, and geographic market.

New features in the Creator Dashboard:
- Real-time click and conversion data (previously 48-hour delay)
- Audience segmentation showing which reader demographics convert at highest rates
- Optimized deep-link generator for specific property types (boutique hotels, apartments, hostels)
- A/B testing tool for comparing link placement performance within newsletter content
- Monthly payout forecasting based on trailing 90-day conversion trends

Beta access is currently limited to affiliates generating 10,000+ monthly unique referrals. Booking.com has indicated general availability is planned for Q3 2026.

For newsletter creators, the dashboard's newsletter-specific tracking is particularly notable — it can attribute conversions to specific email campaigns, allowing creators to identify which newsletter topics drive the highest booking intent among their audience.

Creators interested in beta access can apply through the Booking.com Partner Hub. Priority is being given to creators with demonstrated travel content focus and FTC-compliant disclosure practices.

title: Mediavine Travel RPM Up 15% in Q1 2026 — Programmatic Demand Strengthens for Long-Form Content
summary: Mediavine reports a 15% RPM increase for travel content in Q1 2026 versus Q1 2025, driven by improved programmatic advertiser demand. Long-form destination guides and itinerary content are seeing the strongest RPM gains.
content:
Mediavine's Q1 2026 publisher report shows travel content RPMs up 15% year-over-year, outpacing the network-wide average increase of 9%. The gains are concentrated in long-form content (2,000+ words), with destination guides and multi-day itinerary articles showing the strongest performance.

Key findings:
- Average travel RPM on Mediavine: $28.40 in Q1 2026 vs. $24.70 in Q1 2025
- Long-form content (2,000+ words): RPM up 22% YoY
- Mobile traffic monetization gap narrowing — mobile RPMs now at 78% of desktop (up from 71% in Q1 2025)
- Video ad units within travel articles showing 31% higher RPM than display-only pages

Mediavine attributes the improvement to increased programmatic advertiser spend in the travel vertical, particularly from hotel chains, airline loyalty programs, and travel insurance providers ramping up Q2/Q3 campaign budgets.

For creators considering ad network options, Mediavine's travel-specific performance data reinforces the value of long-form, SEO-optimized destination content as a passive revenue stream alongside newsletter sponsorships and affiliate income.

Mediavine also announced a new 'Travel Creator Cohort' program launching in Q3 2026, offering dedicated account management and RPM optimization support for travel publishers generating 50,000+ monthly sessions.

title: Morocco Press Trip Activity Surges as European Tourism Boards Expand Direct Flight Routes
summary: Morocco's Marrakech and Fes are seeing a surge in press trip activity from European and North American tourism boards, coinciding with new direct flight expansions from Lisbon, London, and Paris. Creator interest in North Africa content is at a multi-year high.
content:
Morocco is experiencing a significant uptick in press trip activity and destination marketing investment, driven by new direct flight routes from major European hubs including Lisbon (TAP Air Portugal), London (easyJet expansion), and Paris (Air France codeshare).

The Lisbon–Marrakech connection is particularly notable for creators already covering Portugal — the 2.5-hour flight makes Morocco a natural extension destination for Portugal-focused content, and several tourism boards are actively seeking creators with established Portuguese-speaking or Iberian-travel audiences.

Press trip activity highlights:
- Moroccan National Tourist Office (ONMT) running a 'Gateway to Africa' creator program through Q3 2026
- Marrakech Riad Association offering hosted stays for creators with 15K+ engaged following
- Fes cultural heritage board partnering with UNESCO on a 'Medina Stories' content initiative

For creators covering the Lisbon–Morocco corridor, the timing aligns with growing audience interest in multi-destination Iberian + North Africa itineraries. Search data shows 'Lisbon to Morocco' queries up 67% YoY.

Content formats performing best for Morocco: immersive food and culture narratives, riad accommodation reviews, and day-trip guides from major European hubs.

title: FTC Reaffirms Disclosure Rules for Newsletter Affiliate Links — 'Clear and Conspicuous' Now Covers Email Footers
summary: The FTC has issued a new enforcement memo clarifying that affiliate link disclosures in email newsletters must appear at or near the point of the link — not solely in footers. Publishers relying on footer-only disclosures are now explicitly at risk of enforcement action. The memo signals a Q3 2026 enforcement ramp-up.
content:
The Federal Trade Commission released an enforcement guidance memo this week reaffirming that its 'clear and conspicuous' disclosure standard applies fully to email newsletters. The memo, addressed to digital publishers and content creators, specifically calls out the practice of placing affiliate disclosures only in email footers as non-compliant when affiliate links appear in the body of the message.

The FTC's position is that a reader scrolling through a newsletter should encounter a disclosure before or at the point they encounter an affiliate link — not after reading the entire email. Footer disclosures may supplement but cannot replace in-body disclosures.

The memo also addresses sponsored content sections within newsletters, requiring that any section containing paid placements be labeled clearly at the top of that section, not just in a general disclaimer elsewhere in the email.

Enforcement actions targeting newsletter publishers are expected to increase in Q3 2026. The FTC has indicated it will prioritize cases where affiliate revenue is material to the publisher's income and where disclosures are absent or inadequate.

Creators and publishers are advised to audit their current newsletter templates and affiliate link placement practices before June 30, 2026.

title: Portugal Tourism Board Prioritizes Newsletter Creators for Q2–Q3 Press Trips — Lisbon and Algarve Lead Demand
summary: Turismo de Portugal has confirmed a 28% increase in inbound press trip requests for 2026, with Lisbon and the Algarve Coast leading. The board is shifting its creator mix toward newsletter and long-form content publishers, citing higher destination conversion rates compared to pure social influencer campaigns.
content:
Turismo de Portugal, the national tourism authority, confirmed this week that inbound press trip requests for 2026 are up 28% year-over-year, with Lisbon and the Algarve Coast accounting for the majority of creator partnership inquiries.

In a notable strategic shift, the board announced it is prioritizing newsletter publishers and long-form content creators over social-only influencers for Q2 and Q3 partnerships. A spokesperson cited internal data showing that destination-specific editorial content in newsletters drives measurably higher booking conversion rates than Instagram or TikTok posts alone.

Visit Lisbon, the city's dedicated tourism marketing arm, has been particularly active in this space, running a structured press trip program through its partnerships team. The program includes sponsored itinerary access, accommodation, and a defined deliverable framework.

The Algarve Coast, meanwhile, is seeing increased interest from European and North American travel creators following the expansion of direct flight routes from Lisbon, London, and Frankfurt. Several regional tourism operators have launched creator partnership programs with Q2 and Q3 availability.

For travel content creators with newsletter audiences, Portugal represents one of the highest-demand destination partnership opportunities in the current cycle.

title: Booking.com Affiliate Creator Dashboard Beta — Real-Time Conversion Tracking Now Available
summary: Booking.com has launched a beta affiliate dashboard for creators with real-time conversion tracking, replacing the previous 48–72 hour reporting delay. The beta is open to creators in the Booking.com Creator Program with at least 90 days of affiliate history.
content:
Booking.com has rolled out a beta version of its Affiliate Creator Dashboard, introducing real-time conversion tracking for participating creators. The update addresses a long-standing complaint from travel content creators who previously had to wait 48 to 72 hours to see click and booking data — a lag that made it difficult to optimize content performance in real time.

The new dashboard displays clicks, bookings, and estimated commissions with a delay of under 15 minutes. It also introduces a content attribution feature that allows creators to tag specific newsletter issues, blog posts, or social posts as the source of a link click, enabling more granular performance analysis.

The beta is currently open to creators enrolled in the Booking.com Creator Program who have at least 90 days of affiliate history on the platform. Booking.com has indicated a full rollout is planned for Q3 2026.

For newsletter publishers, the real-time dashboard is particularly useful for tracking performance of affiliate links included in weekly sends, allowing same-day optimization of follow-up content or social amplification.

Creators interested in joining the beta can apply through the Booking.com Partner Hub.

title: Visit Scotland Open Call: Creators for Highland & Islands Itinerary — Deadline May 28
summary: Visit Scotland has issued an open call for travel content creators to cover a Highland & Islands itinerary in summer 2026. The deadline to apply is May 28. Requirements include 10K+ newsletter subscribers or 25K+ social following, with deliverables including two long-form pieces and an Instagram reel series.
content:
Visit Scotland has launched an open call for travel content creators to participate in a sponsored Highland & Islands itinerary program running in summer 2026. The program is designed for creators who produce long-form destination content, with a preference for newsletter publishers and travel writers.

Eligibility requirements:
- Newsletter: 10,000+ subscribers, OR
- Social media: 25,000+ combined following across Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube
- Demonstrated experience covering European destinations
- Portfolio of at least three published destination pieces in the past 12 months

Deliverables:
- Two long-form destination articles (minimum 1,200 words each) published within 60 days of the trip
- One Instagram reel series (minimum 3 reels) published during or within 14 days of the trip
- One newsletter feature dedicated to the Highland & Islands itinerary

The trip covers accommodation, transportation within Scotland, and select dining experiences. Flights to Edinburgh or Glasgow are not covered.

Applications are due by May 28, 2026. Creators should submit a portfolio link, audience metrics, and a brief pitch (200 words max) via the Visit Scotland Creator Partnership portal.

This is one of several open calls currently active from European national tourism boards targeting English-language travel content creators.

title: Portugal's Algarve Region Sees 34% Surge in Creator Press Trip Requests — Tourism Board Expands Q3 Program
summary: The Algarve Tourism Board has expanded its creator press trip program for Q3 2026 following a 34% spike in inbound requests. Priority is given to newsletter-first creators with engaged audiences over 5,000 subscribers. Contracts now include updated transparency clauses aligned with EU disclosure standards.
content: Following a record Q1 for inbound tourism inquiries, the Algarve Tourism Board announced an expanded creator press trip program for Q3 2026. The board cited a 34% year-over-year increase in creator partnership requests, driven largely by newsletter-first and long-form content creators. A spokesperson noted that new contract templates have been revised to align with EU disclosure standards, removing non-disclosure clauses that had drawn criticism from creator advocacy groups. Priority slots are reserved for creators with newsletter audiences above 5,000 engaged subscribers. Applications open June 1.

title: Affiliate Network Consolidation: Roam & Earn Acquires Two Boutique Travel Programs — Premium Tier Pricing Under Review
summary: Roam & Earn has completed acquisition of two boutique travel affiliate programs, signaling a push toward premium placement packages. Industry analysts warn that pricing for premium tiers may increase post-integration, making current placement windows attractive for early adopters.
content: Roam & Earn confirmed this week the acquisition of two boutique travel affiliate programs — Horizon Trails Affiliate and WanderLink Pro — in a move analysts say positions the network as a dominant player in the mid-tier creator affiliate space. The acquisitions bring an estimated 1,200 additional creator accounts under the Roam & Earn umbrella. Premium placement packages, currently offered at a fixed Q2 rate, are expected to be repriced following integration, which is projected to complete by late Q3 2026. Creators currently evaluating the premium tier are advised to lock in Q2 pricing before the placement window closes. Commission structures for standard tiers remain unchanged.

title: FTC Issues Supplemental Guidance on Sponsored Travel Content — Press Trip Disclosures Must Appear in All Derivative Posts
summary: The FTC released supplemental guidance clarifying that disclosure obligations for sponsored press trips extend to all derivative content — including newsletter issues, social posts, and blog articles — published within 90 days of the trip, even if individual pieces are not directly compensated.
content: The Federal Trade Commission released supplemental guidance on May 15 clarifying the scope of disclosure requirements for sponsored travel content. The guidance specifies that when a creator attends a press trip funded by a tourism board or brand, all derivative content published within 90 days — including newsletter issues, social media posts, and blog articles referencing the destination — must carry a clear and conspicuous disclosure of the sponsorship relationship, regardless of whether individual pieces carry direct compensation. The FTC noted that 'material connection' includes complimentary travel, accommodation, and meals. Creators are advised to update their disclosure templates and newsletter footers accordingly. The guidance takes effect immediately.

title: Southeast Asia Overtakes Mediterranean as Top Creator Destination Pitch in Q2 2026 — Brand Survey
summary: A new brand survey finds Southeast Asia has overtaken the Mediterranean as the most-pitched creator destination for Q2 2026 partnerships, with Vietnam and Thailand leading. Mediterranean destinations including Portugal and Spain remain strong for Q3 pipeline.
content: A quarterly brand survey conducted by Travel PR Wire found that Southeast Asia — led by Vietnam, Thailand, and Indonesia — has overtaken the Mediterranean as the most-pitched creator destination for Q2 2026 brand partnerships. Survey respondents cited lower cost-per-engagement and growing audience appetite for off-the-beaten-path content. Mediterranean destinations, including Portugal, Spain, and Greece, remain dominant in Q3 pipeline projections, with Portugal specifically cited by 38% of tourism board respondents as a priority for newsletter creator partnerships. The survey covered 142 brand and tourism board respondents across North America and Europe.
